title: Taiwan's Golden Melody Nominations Are Out, and Mainland Artists Are on the List Again
excerpt: Su Yunying is up for both Best New Artist and Best Female Mandarin Singer, while Cui Jian and his album *Frozen Light* came away with nothing.
body:
Su Yunying is up for both Best New Artist and Best Female Mandarin Singer, while Cui Jian and his album *Frozen Light* came away with nothing.

On the afternoon of May 13, the 27th Golden Melody Awards published its list of nominees. As in the past few years, plenty of mainland Chinese musicians are on it.

Run since 1990 by the Government Information Office of Taiwan's Executive Yuan, the Golden Melody Awards are the biggest music prizes in Taiwan; together with the Golden Bell Awards for television and the Golden Horse Awards for film, they make up Taiwan's three big annual awards. Carried by the reach of Taiwanese pop, the Golden Melody has also long been one of the most important music awards in the Mandarin-speaking world.

The mainland music scene has never had an awards show with any real authority, so in recent years many mainland musicians have treated the Golden Melody as the place to prove themselves, and have put it on their calendars. At the ceremonies of the past few years, mainland artists including Li Jian, Li Ronghao and Chang Shilei have already won.

This year Cui Jian joined the race too, entering his album *Frozen Light*. In all, 192 acts, 482 albums and 11,177 works were submitted, and 128 works ended up nominated across 26 categories. Cui Jian's new album was not among them, in any category.

![](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702140730bY1UFrPCRGQnL0SJ.jpg-w600)

For the sake of Chinese rock, he has over the years made a phone, made films, staged a dance drama, gone on reality shows, and most recently released his own app. Apart from showing well on the reality shows *I Am a Singer* and *China Star*, none of it has amounted to much. This time he and *Frozen Light* have lost again.

Mainland artists did well enough in this round of nominations, though. Huang Qishan is up for Best Female Mandarin Singer, Li Jian for Best Male Mandarin Singer, and Su Yunying for both Best New Artist and Best Female Mandarin Singer — the happiest surprise among mainland artists so far.

Su Yunying was the runner-up in the second season of *Sing My Song*. Her own song "Wild Child" won Most Noteworthy Song of the Year at the 16th Chinese Music Media Awards, and she was named Best New Artist at the 16th Music Billboard annual ceremony.

![](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702140731L1RAwJh3QtleX89H.jpg-w600)

The biggest winners in this round, though, were still Taiwanese. A-Mei and Sodagreen both made the lists for Song of the Year and Album of the Year, and each also picked up a nomination in their own category — Best Female Mandarin Singer for A-Mei, Best Band for Sodagreen. Sodagreen's *Winter Endless* led the field with eight nominations.

For mainland artists, entering the Golden Melody really is hard. Under the entry rules, a submitted work has to be released first in Taiwan, or released there at the same time as on the mainland — which means a mainland artist must put the album out in Taiwan through an overseas agent, and arrange a Taiwan launch.

That does shape how mainland artists do overall. Two years ago, at the 27th Golden Melody Awards, the mainland artists who fared best on the nomination list were Li Jian and Li Ronghao. But the mainland singer who made the most noise in Taiwan that year was neither of them — it was Song Dongye. His album *North of Anhe Bridge*, however, came out on the mainland long before it reached Taiwan, which left him unable to enter at all.
